title: Endpoint Harmonization: Client Migration Spec and Backstop Criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD-level migration spec to harmonize multiple older inference endpoints and protocol variants (long-poll, multiplexed polling, legacy streaming adapters) into the Unified Inference protocol. Goal: reduce surface area for SDKs and third-party clients, eliminate duplicated routing and fallback logic, and provide deterministic rollback/backstop criteria. This doc covers scope, non-goals, acceptance criteria, instrumentation and telemetry gates, SDK and CLI deliverables, docs and customer communications, and success metrics. It explicitly avoids requiring customers to reimplement business logic in day-one migrations by providing shims and short-lived adapters for high-risk clients.
non_goals: Not a full rewrite of the client SDKs - we will provide adapter layers and a migration CLI
Not removing model aliases -- model alias sunset handled in a separate initiative
Not mandating on-prem runtime upgrades for dedicated customers in phase 1
acceptance_criteria: All production traffic paths for 95% of clients route to unified-inference protocol or behind a compatibility adapter
SDKs (JS, Python, Go) publish stable adapters and non-breaking API calls documented in migration guide
Automated telemetry detects errors introduced by migration with a rollback trigger: >=2x client error rate or >3% user-facing error uplift over baseline for 30m
Canary rollout across 3 customers with increasing traffic windows (1%, 10%, 50%) completed without triggering rollback gates
Operator playbook documented with exact steps for rollback, client opt-out, and emergency model pinning
Migration CLI and one-button console migration for eligible customers exist and pass end-to-end acceptance tests
migration_steps: Inventory of active clients and endpoints (by alias, SDK version, and transport) - engineering to deliver CSV
Implement compatibility adapter service to translate legacy polling/streaming to unified protocol
Add telemetry hooks: per-client error-rate, latency p50/p95, token cost delta, and model-fallback occurrences
Release SDK adapters and migration CLI (v0.1) with feature flag enable/disable
Publish customer migration guide and partner-runbook; schedule webinars for top 50 customers
Canary rollouts with staged traffic ramps and monitoring runbooks
Gradual traffic cutover, with certified auto-rollback triggers enforced in routing layer
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dry-run on staging with simulated traffic and synthetic clients - target date 2026-03-22
Phase 1: Opt-in pilot customers (5 low-risk customers) - target start 2026-04-05
Phase 2: High-value customer pilots + SDK adoption window (30 days) - start 2026-04-20
Phase 3: Automated migration tool available and self-serve console option - target 2026-05-01
Phase 4: Legacy adapter runs as fallback for remaining customers for 90 days post-cutover
timeline: 2026-03-01: PRD approved by API PM tribe
2026-03-10: Compatibility adapter design doc reviewed and accepted
risks: Undiscovered client implementations that rely on transport-level behavior (edge cases in streaming semantics)
Telemetry gaps for customers using private deployments (VPC/on-prem) that delay detection of regressions
Performance regression for latency-sensitive workloads if adapter adds serialization overhead
Insufficient communication causing large customers to miss migration windows leading to manual rollouts
decisions: Provide compatibility adapter as a short-lived bridge rather than forcing immediate client code changes
Enforce telemetry rollback gates at the routing layer (operator-controlled), not client-side
Require security review and additional HSM/KMS scoping for any migration tooling that touches customer keys
open_questions: Which SDK versions will be auto-updated by the console migration tool vs requiring manual client updates?
How do we prioritize customers in the pilot cohort if they use a mix of dedicated and hosted deployments?
Do we support a grace period for clients to opt out with a feature flag longer than 90 days for enterprise customers?
